paper.title_en: CE\(\nu\)NS search with cryogenic sapphire detectors at MINER: From TRIGA results to HFIR prospects$^\star$
paper.abstract_en: Coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering (CE<math altimg="si101.svg" display="inline" id="d1e407"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS) is a sensitive probe of low-energy neutrino interactions but requires ultra-low thresholds and backgrounds. The MINER experiment deployed cryogenic sapphire (<math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e413"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Al</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>) detectors with TES readout at the <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e431"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">MW</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">th</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> TRIGA reactor, achieving a <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e446"><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow></math> eV baseline resolution with a 72 g detector. Analysis of 158 and <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e454"><mrow><mn>381</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">days</mi></mrow></math> reactor-ON and OFF data shows no CE<math altimg="si101.svg" display="inline" id="d1e466"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS excess (<math altimg="si7.svg" display="inline" id="d1e472"><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>53</mn></mrow></math>, where <math altimg="si8.svg" display="inline" id="d1e487"><mi>ρ</mi></math> is the ratio between the experimentally measured and theoretically predicted SM CE<math altimg="si101.svg" display="inline" id="d1e492"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS cross-section), indicating background-dominated measurements. To improve sensitivity, MINER will move to the <math altimg="si10.svg" display="inline" id="d1e497"><mrow><mn>85</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">MW</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">th</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> HFIR at Oak Ridge, benefiting from <math altimg="si11.svg" display="inline" id="d1e511"><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>70</mn></mrow></math> times higher flux, improved shielding, and increased detector mass. The upgraded setup is expected to reach <math altimg="si12.svg" display="inline" id="d1e520"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow></math> sensitivity with <math altimg="si13.svg" display="inline" id="d1e528"><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>30</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">kg</mi><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">days</mi></mrow></math> exposure and enable precision reactor CE<math altimg="si101.svg" display="inline" id="d1e542"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS measurements.
